sanskrit: namas te jāyamānāyai jātāyā uta te namaḥ | bālebhyaḥ śaphebhyo rūpāyāghnye te namaḥ ||
english: Homage to you at your coming-to-birth, and homage to you when born. To your tender parts, to your hooves, to your form, O inviolable cow — homage to you.

sanskrit: yo vidyāt sapta pravataḥ sapta vidyāt parāvataḥ | śiro yajñasya yo vidyāt sa vaśāṃ prati gṛhṇīyāt ||
english: He who knows the seven near reaches, who knows the seven far reaches, he who knows the head of the sacrifice — he shall receive the cow as his due.

sanskrit: vedāhaṃ sapta pravataḥ sapta veda parāvataḥ | śiro yajñasyāhaṃ veda somaṃ cāsyāṃ vicakṣaṇam ||
english: I know the seven near reaches, I know the seven far reaches; I know the head of the sacrifice, and the discerning Soma that dwells within her.

sanskrit: yayā dyaur yayā pṛthivī yayāpo gupitā imāḥ | vaśāṃ sahasradhārāṃ brahmaṇācchā vadāmasi ||
english: By her are heaven and earth sustained, by her these waters are guarded — the cow of a thousand streams, her we address with sacred formulas.

sanskrit: śataṃ vatsāḥ śataṃ dogdhāraḥ śataṃ goptāro adhi pṛṣṭhe asyāḥ | ye devās tasyāṃ prāṇanti te vaśāṃ vidur ekadhā ||
english: A hundred calves, a hundred milkers, a hundred guardians upon her back — the gods who breathe within her, they know the cow as the one undivided whole.

sanskrit: yajñapadīrākṣīrā svadhāprāṇā mahīlukā | vaśā parjanyapatnī devām̐ apyeti brahmaṇā ||
english: She whose footstep is the sacrifice, whose eye is the oblation, whose breath is the ancestral offering, the great and luminous one — the cow, Parjanya's wife, approaches the gods through sacred formulas.

sanskrit: anu tvāgniḥ prāviśad anu somo vaśe tvā | ūdhas te bhadre parjanyo vidyutas te stanā vaśe ||
english: Agni entered into you, Soma followed you, O cow. Parjanya is your udder, O auspicious one, the lightnings are your teats, O cow.

sanskrit: apas tvaṃ dhukṣe prathamā urvarā aparā vaśe | tṛtīyaṃ rāṣṭraṃ dhukṣe annaṃ kṣīraṃ vaśe tvam ||
english: You milk the waters first, then the arable land, O cow; thirdly you milk sovereignty — food and milk you give, O cow.

sanskrit: yad ādityair hūyamānā- -upatiṣṭha ṛtāvari | indraḥ sahasraṃ pātraiḥ somaṃ tvāpāyayad vaśe ||
english: When, being invoked by the Ādityas, you stood present, O guardian of truth, Indra made you drink Soma in a thousand vessels, O cow.

sanskrit: yad anūcīndram air āt tva ṛṣabho 'hvayat | tasmāt te vṛtrahā payaḥ kṣīraṃ kruddho 'bharad vaśe ||
english: When, turning away from Indra, the bull called out to you — then the slayer of Vṛtra, enraged, brought you milk and cream, O cow.

sanskrit: yat te kruddho dhanapatiḥ kṣīraṃ te abharad vaśe | idaṃ tad adya nākas triṣu pātreṣu rakṣati ||
english: That milk which the lord of wealth, though enraged, brought to you, O cow — that very milk the vault of heaven today protects in three vessels.

sanskrit: triṣu pātreṣu taṃ somam ā devy abharad vaśā | atharvā yatra dīkṣito barhiṣy āsta hiraṇyaye ||
english: In three vessels the divine cow brought that Soma — where Atharvan, consecrated, sat upon the golden sacrificial grass.

sanskrit: saṃ hi somenāgata sam u sarveṇa padvatā | vaśā samudre prānartīd ṛcaḥ sāmāni bibhratī ||
english: She came together with Soma and with all that moves on feet; the cow danced before the ocean, bearing the Ṛc and Sāman hymns.

sanskrit: saṃ hi sūryeṇāgata sam u sarveṇa cakṣuṣā | vaśā samudram aty aṣṭhād gandharvaiḥ kalibhiḥ saha ||
english: She came together with the Sun and with all that has sight; the cow strode beyond the ocean together with the Gandharvas and the Kalis.

sanskrit: saṃ hi vātenāgata sam u sarvaiḥ patatribhiḥ | vaśā samudram aty akhyad bhadrā jyotīṃṣi bibhratī ||
english: She came together with the Wind and with all winged creatures; the auspicious cow surveyed beyond the ocean, bearing the celestial lights.

sanskrit: tad bhadrāḥ sam agacchanta vaśā deṣṭry atho svadhā | atharvā yatra dīkṣito barhiṣy āsta hiraṇyaye ||
english: Then the auspicious things came together — the cow as guide, and also the ancestral oblation — where Atharvan, consecrated, sat upon the golden sacrificial grass.

sanskrit: abhīvṛtā hiraṇyena yad atiṣṭha ṛtāvari | aśvaḥ samudro bhūtvā- -adhy askandad vaśe tvā ||
english: When you stood there, covered with gold, O guardian of truth, the ocean, having become a horse, leaped upon you, O cow.

sanskrit: vaśā mātā rājanyasya vaśā mātā svadhe tava | vaśāyā jajña āyudhaṃ tataś cittam ajāyata ||
english: The cow is the mother of the royal caste, the cow is your mother, O ancestral libation. From the cow was born the weapon, and from that arose thought.

sanskrit: ūrdhvo bindur ud acarad brahmaṇaḥ kakudād adhi | tatas tvaṃ jajñiṣe vaśe tato hotā ajāyata ||
english: The upward drop moved aloft, from the hump of brahman — from that you were born, O cow; from that the Hotṛ priest was born.

sanskrit: āsnas te gāthā bhavantu- -uṣṇihābhyo balaṃ tava | pājasyāj jajñe te yajña stanebhyo raśmayo vaśe ||
english: Let the sacred songs be born from your mouth; your strength comes from the Uṣṇih metres. From your girth the sacrifice was born, from your teats the rays of light, O cow.

sanskrit: īrmābhyām ayanaṃ jātaṃ sakthibhyāṃ ca vaśe tava | āntrebhyo atrā jajñira udarād adhi vīrudhaḥ ||
english: From your shoulder-joints and your haunches, O cow, the path was born; from your entrails the food was produced, from your belly the plants sprang up.

sanskrit: yad udaraṃ varuṇasya- -anu prāviśathā vaśe | tatas tvā brahmodahvayat sa hi netram avet tava ||
english: When you entered into Varuṇa's belly, O cow, then the sacred formulation called you out — for he it was who found your eye.

sanskrit: sarve garbhād avepanta jāyamānād asūsvaḥ | sasūva hi tām āhur vaśeti brahmaṇā kl̥pta uta bandhur asyāḥ ||
english: All trembled at her birth, at the one being born from the womb — for she has given birth; they call her the cow, fashioned by sacred formulas, and she is a kinswoman to all.

sanskrit: yudha ekaḥ saṃ sṛjati yo asyā eka id vaśī | tarāṃsi yajñā abhavan tarasāṃ cakṣur abhavad vaśā ||
english: The one who alone is the master of her joins together in battle; the swift-moving sacrifices came into being, the cow became the eye of the swift-moving ones.

sanskrit: vaśā sūryaṃ praty agṛhṇād vaśā yajñam adhārayat | vaśāyām antar āviśad odano brahmaṇā saha ||
english: The cow took hold of the Sun, the cow sustained the sacrifice; into the cow there entered the odana rice-cooked oblation along with sacred formulas.

sanskrit: vaśām evāhur amṛtaṃ vaśāṃ mṛtyum upāsate | vaśedaṃ sarvam abhavad devā manuṣyā asurāḥ pitara ṛṣayaḥ ||
english: The cow alone they call immortality; the cow they worship as death. All this became the cow — gods, humans, Asuras, the ancestors, and the seers.

sanskrit: ya evaṃ vidyāt sa vaśāṃ prati gṛhṇīyāt | tathā hi yajñaḥ sarvapād duhe dātre anapasphuran ||
english: He who knows thus shall receive the cow as his due — for in this way the sacrifice, complete on all feet, yields milk to the giver without withholding.

sanskrit: tisro jihvā varuṇasya- -antar didyaty āsani | tāsāṃ yā madhye rājati sa vaśā duṣpratigrahā ||
english: Three tongues of Varuṇa flash within the mouth; among them the one that shines in the middle — she is the cow, hard to receive.

sanskrit: caturdhā reto abhavad vaśāyā apas turīyam amṛtaṃ turīyaṃ yajñas turīyaṃ paśavas turīyam | ya evaṃ vidyāt sa vaśāṃ prati gṛhṇīyāt ||
english: The seed of the cow became fourfold: one quarter is the waters, one quarter immortality, one quarter the sacrifice, one quarter the animals. He who knows thus shall receive the cow as his due.

sanskrit: vaśā dyaur vaśā pṛthivī vaśā viṣṇuḥ prajāpatiḥ | vaśāyā dugdham apiban sādhyā vasavaś ca ye ||
english: The cow is heaven, the cow is earth, the cow is Viṣṇu and Prajāpati. The Sādhyas and the Vasus drank the milk drawn from the cow.
